fingerprint_guidance: Resolve raw MP4 member names, source recording IDs and frame stems to one canonical recording before comparing files. a3_train1 frame stems and a3_train_1.mp4 may represent the same recording; archive member mappings must be explicit.

A different frame index, timestamp, crop, resize, JPEG quality or video re-encode is not independent data. Treat all adjacent segments from a known training or development recording as that same exposed source.

Compare original-source file SHA256 where available, saved derivative file SHA256, decoded RGB SHA256 with dimensions and exact decode/preprocessing definition, then near-duplicate sequence/visual matching. Hash mismatches only exclude exact equality.

The provided EXP009 pixel hashes are of decoded saved max1280 JPEG90 derivatives. Raw-video frames will need the same documented transformation for exact comparison, and re-encoding may prevent exact matches even for identical content.

Use timestamp sequence alignment and provenance before perceptual similarity. Physically repeated pieces across different recordings require independent IDs or model-blind human audit; visual distance alone is not proof of disjointness.

A frozen source ZIP central-directory index lists reserved source members and CRCs; its mere existence does not imply test pixel/label access. Separate index creation, file acquisition, label reading, prediction generation and result-driven selection in the exposure ledger.
A fresh score run on previously exposed footage is a reproducibility or robustness result. Describe independently audited evaluation separately from untouched independent-data evaluation.

A3 publisher-test is now confirmed historically exposed by saved-image/manifest and saved-prediction evidence. A1 test is also historically exposed. A2/A4/A5 need their own use history plus cross-subset piece mapping; do not assume that a previously unopened file is an independent physical-object holdout.
